properties.decision:
From `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-26`, opportunity O-01 — the report's own top priority, raised from a real program rather than from thinking about reflow2.

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ THE USE CASE, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE REFLOW2 WAS BUILT FOR ═══

*"`hxm_program` is not a product; it is a hub — a living, agent-maintained source of truth for a program of beamlines whose actual code lives in ~10 other repos... The graph is used less as 'the design of a system' and more as the program's memory and coherence engine."*

**Eight `.reflow2` stores on one machine**: the hub, two sim-scoped sub-designs (one of which has since moved into a *different* repo), a vision design, three unrelated projects, and reflow2's own. Only one person runs reflow2; ~6 collaborators read markdown.

═══ THE GAP, STATED PRECISELY ═══

Two designs can today **LINK as peers** (`published`/`required` boundaries, `pair_designs`, `seam_report`, `mirror_surface`) or **MERGE** (absorption). The hub needs a third: *this design is the hub of those* — ownership and roll-up **without absorption**. Four things it wants to say, none of which the current vocabulary expresses:

1. *"Capability X here **is realised by** their design"* — a cross-design REALIZES/SATISFIES, **so the hub stops keeping shadow copies of the sim's capabilities, which it does today and nothing flags the duplication**
2. *"When their committed export moves, tell me"* — `sync_status` against ANOTHER design's export
3. *"Roll their verification state up"* — the hub's `loop_status` showing the children's pass/fail without owning those checks
4. `describe_designs` reporting each design's **last export date**, so a hub can see which children have gone dark

⭐ AND THE REASON IT IS NOT AN INTERFACE PROBLEM, in their words: *"the seam vocabulary (medium, auth, payload, error model) fits interfaces; the hub's relations are dependency/ownership, and forcing them into `Interface` nodes would be modelling fiction."* **That is the argument, and it is a good one** — reflow2's contract vocabulary describes what two systems must agree on at a boundary, which is a different relation from one design being answerable for another.

═══ 🛑 THE OBJECTION THAT MUST BE MET FIRST, AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S STANDING ONE ═══

**Is a hub-of-designs a design brain, or a programme-management tool?** The same objection killed the Task node type on 2026-08-25 (*"this is the road to being a tracker"*) and shadows the MCP-contract idea recorded the same day. Roll-up, ownership and portfolio status are recognisably PPM features, and every step toward being good at that is a step toward being worse at holding WHY.

⭐ **THE COUNTER, AND IT IS WHY THIS ONE MAY EARN ITS PLACE:** item 1 is not portfolio reporting, it is a **coherence** claim — *the hub is keeping shadow copies of another design's capabilities and nothing detects the duplication*. That is exactly the class of thing reflow2 exists to catch, and it is invisible today. Items 2–4 are reporting; item 1 is the design brain failing at its own job across a boundary it cannot see.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen (the report records link / merge / index / hybrid with costs) ═══

**(a) A cross-design REALIZES/SATISFIES only.** Solve item 1 alone — the coherence half — and leave roll-up out. Smallest, and it attacks the one thing that is a design defect rather than a status report. ⚠️ Counter: needs a way to name a node in another design that survives that design moving repo, which is `dec:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` territory and not free.

**(b) An index/registry design that knows about others.** `describe_designs` already reads sidecars safely without minting. Extend to last-export-date and a declared parent. ⚠️ Counter: filesystem-scoped, so it works on one machine and not for a hub whose children are in other people's repos.

**(c) Full hub relation with roll-up.** What the report asks for. ⚠️ Counter: the tracker objection lands hardest here, and roll-up of verification state means the hub reports numbers it cannot verify — a `report-dont-judge` problem.

**(d) Do nothing; say the hub case is out of scope.** ⚠️ Counter: it is a real user with a real program, and `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` says field use is the point. Declining should be explicit rather than by neglect.

📌 **PREREQUISITE THE REPORT NAMES ITSELF (O-02):** *zero of seven sibling designs on that machine has a committed export or a published surface*, and `link-projects` correctly forbids opening a sibling's store. **So none of this is reachable until partners export** — which is a nudge problem (their F-07: *"there is no export at all" is still silent*) before it is a vocabulary problem.
properties.name: OPEN — a design can LINK to a peer or MERGE with one; hxm_program needs a third thing — to be the HUB of others, with roll-up and ownership but no absorption
properties.rationale:
Recorded because it is the report's own top priority, it comes from live program work rather than from reflow2's development, and the gap it names is real: the vocabulary genuinely has link and merge and nothing between them.

The tracker objection is written in at full strength rather than as a caveat, because it is the objection that has already killed one adjacent idea in this design and would apply here unexamined. What distinguishes this case is item 1 — undetected shadow copies across a design boundary — which is a coherence failure rather than a reporting gap, and is the only part of the request that reflow2 is uniquely placed to answer.

The O-02 prerequisite is recorded on the node rather than left in the report, because it changes the ORDER: no hub relation is usable while zero siblings export, so the cheap nudge may unblock more than the expensive vocabulary would.
